newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Hibernian 1996 new life/pensions sales up.
newsitem.headline: Hibernian 1996 new life/pensions sales up.

text.p: Ireland's Hibernian Group Plc said on Thursay its new annual premium life and business sales rose nine percent in 1996 to 12.076 million punts.
Pensions business was up 20 percent on the previous year at 7.770 million punts while life assurance business declined to 4.306 million from 4.584 million.

Pensions single premium business grew by two percent to 17.258 million while life single premiums fell to 2.281 million from 7.393 million, reflecting Hibernian's decision not to participate in the tracker bond market, the company said.

Chief executive Adrian Daly said in a statement that Hibernian had increased its focus on pensions business over the past three years, laying "firm foundations for the strong growth in pensions sales now evident".
"Hibernian has led the way in offering better, more flexible and more transparent pension products and we will continue with that development," he said.
Hibernian said its products had performed well in the independent broker market.
"Business from independent brokers increased by 15 percent in 1996 and continues to be Hibernian's primary distribution channel," it said.
